title: Good Friday
hook: John's passion, prayers for the whole world, and the veneration of the cross
carry: behold the wood of the cross

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Mandatum: a towel, a basin, and the new commandment. Your line was love one another.

Three o'clock on a Friday afternoon. People in the pews, and almost no sound. The altar is bare. No bells, no opening song. The priest and ministers walk in without a word, and then the priest does something you won't see on an ordinary Sunday: he lies face down on the floor, or kneels, and stays there in silence. Nobody explains it. Everyone waits. Today, in the Roman Rite, there is no Mass at all.
screen: `THREE O'CLOCK, ALMOST NO SOUND.` → `FACE DOWN ON THE FLOOR.` → `NO MASS TODAY.`

segments.voice: The service, often at three in the afternoon, the hour Jesus died, has three parts. First, the readings: Isaiah's suffering servant, wounded for our iniquities, and then, every year, the Passion from John's gospel, often read in parts. John's Jesus is strikingly calm. In the garden, when the soldiers come, he steps forward and says, I am he, and they fall back. He carries his own cross. From it he gives his mother and his beloved disciple to each other. And his last words, in the Douay-Rheims, are: "It is consummated." Finished, completed, the work done. Then the second part, the Solemn Intercessions: ten long prayers for the whole world. For the Church and the pope, for those preparing for baptism, for Christian unity, for the Jewish people, for those who don't believe in Christ or in God, for leaders, and for everyone who suffers. Nobody is left out. Then the third part. A cross is carried up the aisle, unveiled in stages or carried in procession, and the priest sings in the old Latin: "Ecce lignum Crucis." Behold the wood of the cross, on which hung the salvation of the world. Come, let us adore. And people come forward one by one to genuflect, touch, or kiss the wood. Communion follows, from hosts consecrated the night before, and everyone leaves in silence. Catholics fast today. And why call it good? Some say the word once carried a sense close to holy. Catholics call it good because of what they believe was finished on the cross.
screen: `JOHN'S PASSION: I AM HE.` · `IT IS CONSUMMATED.` · `TEN PRAYERS FOR THE WORLD.` · `ECCE LIGNUM CRUCIS.` · then, large: `BEHOLD THE WOOD OF THE CROSS.`

segments.voice: If there's a crucifix in your home, a cross on a chain, or one in a church you can reach, hold it, touch it or kiss it the way people do at the veneration; if you have none, trace one on your palm with a finger. Then sit in silence, the way the church does today, and let it be heavy if it's heavy. If you pray, whisper the old words, behold the wood of the cross; if you don't, simply stay with the silence.
Good Friday. The day of the Lord's Passion: no Mass, John's Passion, prayers for the whole world, and the veneration of the cross. Today's word.
Your line: behold the wood of the cross. The quiet holds until the Vigil. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: On Good Friday Catholics celebrate the Passion of the Lord, often at 3 p.m., with John's Passion, the Solemn Intercessions, the veneration of the cross and Communion; no Mass is celebrated, and it is a day of fasting and abstinence.

trapdoor: what you thought: it's called good because it was a good day.
what it means: the day of the Passion, kept with no Mass, John's Passion, prayers for all and the veneration of the cross.
what a scholar hears: the Douay-Rheims 'it is consummated' follows the Vulgate's 'consummatum est', which renders the single Greek word tetelestai: finished, the work complete.
recall: servant, as in Isaiah's suffering servant

chat.says: If it's the day Jesus died, why do Catholics call it Good Friday?
options: Because of what they believe was finished on the cross; good may once have meant holy.
Because the fast ends at three o'clock, and the evening turns into a feast.
Because it began as a spring festival that the Church renamed much later.

Roman Rite.meaning: the usual form of worship in the Latin Catholic Church

Solemn Intercessions.meaning: ten long prayers for the Church and the whole world

Ecce lignum Crucis.meaning: Latin: behold the wood of the cross

veneration.meaning: coming forward to honor the cross by a touch, kiss or genuflection

notes: Ten Solemn Intercessions, summarized; confirm the list and that mention of the intercession for the Jewish people is appropriately neutral.
The English 'Behold the wood of the cross, on which hung the salvation of the world. Come, let us adore' is given as a literal rendering of the Latin, not quoted from a copyrighted translation.
Etymology of 'Good' in Good Friday: the 'holy' sense is the prevailing view (vs. 'God's Friday'). Confirm wording.

Prostration may be replaced by kneeling (rubric); hook now says so. Prostration also occurs at ordinations, so the earlier 'no other day of the year' claim was softened to 'not on an ordinary Sunday'. Confirm.
Tetelestai (John 19:30) and the DR 'consummated' (from Vulgate 'consummatum est').
